column3: NASB follows the critical text without “Paul”; it reads “he.”
NASB reorders the verse, rendering “and Priscilla his wife” as “with his wife Priscilla.”
NASB follows the critical text; it reads “they were working,” a plural that some manuscripts have; the critical text has “he was working.”
NASB renders “was persuading” as “trying to persuade.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the word”); “was occupied with” is rendered “began devoting himself completely to.”
NASB renders “denigrating” as “blasphemed” and adds “own.”
NASB follows the critical text with “Titius Justus.”
NASB renders “ruler of the synagogue” as “leader of the synagogue.”
NASB renders the present prohibition as “Do not be afraid any longer.”
NASB renders “lay a hand on” as “attack.” A stray quotation mark appears in the NASB text.
NASB renders “remained” as “settled there.”
NASB renders “led” as “brought.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “unrighteousness” as “wrong” and “I would have endured you” as “it would be reasonable for me to put up with you.”
NASB follows the critical text (“questions”); “you will see to it” is rendered “look after it yourselves.” A stray quotation mark appears in the NASB text.
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text without “the Greeks”; “ruler” is rendered “leader.”
NASB renders “having shaved the head” as “had his hair cut” and “he had a vow” as “he was keeping a vow.”
NASB follows the critical text.
NASB follows the critical text without “with them.”
NASB follows the critical text without the Textus Receptus words about keeping the coming feast in Jerusalem; “God willing” is rendered “if God wills.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB adds “there.”
NASB renders “a native” as “by birth.”
NASB follows the critical text (“Jesus”); it adds “This man” and “being acquainted.”
NASB renders “took him to themselves” as “took him aside.”
NASB renders “resolving” as “wanted” and “pass through” as “go across.”
Close to the Greek.
